title: What Is a Primary?
body: A primary decides which candidate(s) move forward to the general election. In some states, party registration affects which primary ballot you can use.

title: What Is a General Election?
body: The general election chooses who takes office. Depending on state rules, the winner may be decided by plurality or may require a majority threshold.

title: What Is a Runoff?
body: A runoff is a second election round used when no candidate reaches the required threshold in the first round.

title: What To Bring
body: Bring photo ID if available. This jurisdiction is listed in a non-strict photo-ID category with fallback verification paths. If check-in issues occur, ask for a provisional ballot and follow cure instructions if needed.

title: Voting Options
body: Early in-person voting is not listed as open to all voters statewide; eligible absentee pathways may still exist. Mail voting is available by state-defined rules; request and return deadlines vary.

title: Runoff Rule in Your State
body: Primary runoff/second-round rules may apply if thresholds are not met.

title: Election Structure in Your State
body: Election format follows state law for each office (for example plurality, majority-plus-runoff, or other defined structures).
